name: witness
tagline: A recording cache for model APIs that cuts inference spend and resumes crashed runs
summary: witness is a single-binary, API-compatible proxy that sits between your agents and a model API, and agents change only the base URL. Repeat deterministic calls are served from the record instead of re-paying inference, and a crashed run can be replayed with zero model calls. The same record is a tamper-evident, signed, Merkle-committed audit trail, so it is already running as evidence before anyone asks a question.

features: Repeat deterministic calls are served from the record instead of re-paying inference
Whole runs replay from the record with zero upstream calls, so crashed runs resume
Hash-chained journal with Merkle commitments, inclusion proofs and anchoring to a public transparency log
Ed25519 signed identity and narrowing-only delegations enforced at the network boundary
Records MCP tool calls and shell commands by what they changed, in the same chain; fleet peer cache and Prometheus and OpenTelemetry export
how_it_works: Agents point their base URL at witness serve, which forwards to the model API and stores every request and response by BLAKE3 content hash.
Each call is appended to a hash-chained journal, so any edit, deletion or reorder breaks the chain and witness verify finds it.
Identical reusable requests are answered from the record, and witness replay serves a whole recorded run with no upstream calls.
quickstart:
witness serve --port 8787 --upstream https://api.anthropic.com --cache
# then point your agents at http://127.0.0.1:8787 instead of api.anthropic.com

notes: Best hero: assets/demo.gif (1050x620). The 803 ms vs 541µs figures come from the demo run against the built-in mock upstream, which simulates 800 ms of model latency (demo.sh: mock --latency-ms 800); real savings equal the full upstream call skipped. The 0.25 ms and 53k/sec figures come from bench/bench.sh against a zero-latency mock on an M-series MacBook (median of 3 runs, n=2000, c=20). Version 0.3.0 is from the GitHub release tag; Cargo.toml still says 0.1.0. The crates.io crate named 'witness' belongs to someone else, so do not link crates. Release assets are prebuilt tarballs (linux arm64/x86_64, macos arm64/x86_64) with no demo video. The README names several overlapping projects in a prior-art table; the site copy avoids naming them. No cost-saving percentage is published in the README, so none is claimed.
